title: Flat coefficient restriction and normalized derived operations on module diagrams
statement:
Let $J$ be a small category, and let $\mathcal C_U,\mathcal C_V$ be small sites in the module-sheaf universe. Let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_U)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_V)$ be a geometric morphism, that is an adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ with $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. On each site $T=U,V$ let $a_T:R_T\to S_T$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings. Suppose $S_T$ is flat over $R_T$, meaning $S_T\otimes_{R_T}-$ is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Specify ring isomorphisms $c_R:u^{-1}R_V\simeq R_U$ and $c_S:u^{-1}S_V\simeq S_U$ satisfying $a_Uc_R=c_Su^{-1}a_V$. Put $\mathcal A_{T,R}=\operatorname{Fun}(J,\operatorname{Mod}(R_T))$ and $\mathcal A_{T,S}=\operatorname{Fun}(J,\operatorname{Mod}(S_T))$, with module sheaves as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and diagram-site models as in [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Let $r_T$ be termwise restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $L_R,L_S$ be termwise inverse image with the ring action transported by $c_R,c_S$, and $F_R,F_S$ termwise module direct image, whose action uses the adjoint ring map. Use the termwise module adjunctions $L_R\dashv F_R$, $L_S\dashv F_S$. Write $D$ for localization of cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; derive exact functors termwise and derive $F_R,F_S$ by K-injective resolutions, where K-injective means every map from an acyclic complex is null-homotopic [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Use the derived adjunctions normalized by [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general].

Restriction $r_T$ is exact and preserves K-injective diagram complexes. There are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$b:r_UL_S\xrightarrow{\sim}L_Rr_V,\qquad d:r_VRF_S\xrightarrow{\sim}RF_Rr_U.$$
Here $b$ is the termwise identified inverse image on underlying abelian sheaves. For a K-injective complex $I$ in $\mathcal A_{U,S}$, $r_UI$ computes the restricted object's derived image, and $d_{QI}$ is induced by the underived identity $r_VF_SI=F_Rr_UI$ with its identified ring actions; $Q$ is localization. These comparisons respect adjuncts: for $M\in D(\mathcal A_{V,S})$, $N\in D(\mathcal A_{U,S})$, and $t:L_SM\to N$ with adjunct $t^\sharp:M\to RF_SN$, the adjunct of $r_U(t)b_M^{-1}$ is $d_Nr_V(t^\sharp)$. The comparisons are isomorphisms of derived diagram functors, including all $J$-transition maps.

proof.text: Work in the diagram categories themselves. By [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization] they are abelian categories of module sheaves on small diagram sites, and kernels and cokernels are componentwise in $J$. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], a module kernel is the sectionwise kernel and a module cokernel is the sheafification of the sectionwise cokernel. Restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] changes neither underlying abelian sheaf nor maps. The sectionwise kernels have the restricted action. The same underlying cokernel sheaf, with its induced restricted action, is a cokernel after restriction: its universal factorization is linear because the quotient map is locally surjective and the original map is linear. Thus $r_T$ preserves kernels and cokernels and is exact. This also shows that exactness of a sequence of $S_T$-module sheaves is detected after restriction to $R_T$.

source.place: Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian; section on change of rings, Tag 03CZ

proof.text: Define $E_T$ on a diagram $M$ by $(E_TM)(j)=S_T\otimes_{R_T}M(j)$, with the sheaf tensor of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Sectionwise the two maps in [lem-weil-pbc-scalar-extension-hom] send $h$ to $m\mapsto h(1\otimes m)$ and send $f$ to $s\otimes m\mapsto sf(m)$. They commute with site restrictions and diagram arrows: the latter formula applied to $s\otimes M(\alpha)m$ is $s f_k(M(\alpha)m)=sN(\alpha)f_j(m)$. The universal property in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] therefore gives inverse natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(E_TM,N)=\operatorname{Hom}(M,r_TN)$ on diagram sheaves. Hence $E_T\dashv r_T$. The hypothesis [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] says that its underlying $R_T$-module tensor functor is exact; exactness is detected on underlying module sheaves by step 1, and is componentwise in $J$. Consequently $E_T$ is exact as an $S_T$-module-valued functor.

source.place: Tag 03CZ, lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict; flatness as defined in the statement

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] to the additive adjunction $E_T\dashv r_T$ of step 2. Its left adjoint is exact by flatness, and its categories are abelian by step 1. Therefore $r_T$ preserves K-injective complexes of diagrams. This is K-injectivity in the whole diagram category, not an inference from the K-injectivity of separate evaluations.

For $B=R,S$, [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-module-transport], with ring identification $c_B^{-1}$ and structural map the identity of $B_U$, gives the prescribed $L_B\dashv F_B$, whose underlying Hom bijection is the given sheaf adjunction. These Hom bijections commute with every $J$-arrow by their naturality, so restrict to diagram morphisms. The underlying set sheaf of $L_B$ is $u^{-1}$ of the underlying set sheaf. Kernels of module maps are equalizers with the zero map by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; finite-limit preservation of $u^{-1}$ therefore shows that $L_B$ preserves kernels and zero objects. It preserves cokernels as well: maps $L_BN\to H$ killing $L_Bf$ correspond under the adjunction exactly to maps $N\to F_BH$ killing $f$, which factor uniquely through its cokernel. Thus $L_R,L_S$ are exact, also on diagrams. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], $F_R,F_S$ preserve K-injectives.

Construct the ordinary $b^0:r_UL_S\simeq L_Rr_V$ by the identity on the identified underlying $u^{-1}$ sheaves. Its $R_U$-linearity is precisely $a_Uc_R=c_Su^{-1}a_V$. Write $\rho_R:R_V\to u_*R_U$ and $\rho_S:S_V\to u_*S_U$ for the adjoints of $c_R,c_S$. Naturality of the sheaf adjunction gives $u_*(a_U)\rho_R=\rho_Sa_V$. Hence the two $R_V$-actions on the same sheaf $u_*N$ agree: one uses $a_V$ then $\rho_S$ and the other uses $\rho_R$ then $u_*a_U$ before the $S_U$-action. This gives the ordinary comparison $q:r_VF_S\simeq F_Rr_U$, the identity with these actions identified. All identifications on objects and maps are those in [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-module-transport] and [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. They are natural in the module, hence commute with every diagram arrow.

source.place: Tag 03D3, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules; naturality of the underlying adjunction

proof.text:
Let $\eta^R,\eta^S$ be the ordinary units. The normalization in [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-module-transport] says that their underlying sheaf maps are both the unit of $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$. Since $b^0$ and $q$ in step 5 are the identity under those same identifications, faithfulness of the underlying-sheaf functor gives
$$F_R((b^0_M)^{-1})\eta^R_{r_VM}=q_{L_SM}\,r_V(\eta^S_M).$$
For any module diagram map $h:L_SM\to N$, apply $F_Rr_U(h)$ to this equation. Naturality of $q$ gives
$$F_R(r_U(h)(b^0_M)^{-1})\eta^R_{r_VM}
=q_Nr_V(F_S(h)\eta^S_M).$$
These are exactly the ordinary adjunct formulas. By [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] they remain the formulas on complexes and homotopy classes, with the same comparisons $b^0,q$ applied degreewise.

Apply [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] on each small ringed diagram site supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. This gives functorial K-injective resolutions in all four diagram categories. Applying an additive functor to complexes preserves shifts and mapping cones (the cone uses only finite direct sums and the differential matrix), so its functor from the homotopy category to the target derived category is exact triangulated. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] supplies $RF_R,RF_S$ and their normalized computation isomorphisms on K-injectives. For the exact functors $r_T,L_R,L_S$ use [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]: their termwise localizations compute their derived functors on every complex. In particular, localizing $b^0$ gives the required $b$. These are the representing data that [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] requires. For $F=F_R,F_S$ let $\beta:QF_h\to RF\,Q$ be the comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], invertible on K-injectives. For a complex $K$ and a quasi-isomorphism $s:K\to I'$ put $p_s=RF(Qs)^{-1}\beta_{I'}$, a cocone by naturality of $\beta$. Fix a K-injective resolution $s_0:K\to I_0$ and $\rho=\beta_{I_0}^{-1}RF(Qs_0)$, so $p_{s_0}\rho=1$. Given $s$, filteredness and a further K-injective resolution give $s_k:K\to I_k$, $I_k$ K-injective, with $a:I_0\to I_k$, $c:I'\to I_k$ under $K$; naturality of $\beta$ at $a$ and invertibility of $\beta_{I_k}$ give $QF_h(a)\rho p_s=QF_h(c)$, the transition map. So $p$ exhibits the ind-system as essentially constant [def-pc-essentially-constant-ind-diagram]; for K-injective $K$ and $s=\mathrm{id}$, $p_{\mathrm{id}}=\beta_K$. Dually, for $G=L_R,L_S$ with comparison $\varphi:G_DQ\simeq QG$ and a quasi-isomorphism $t:P\to M$, put $u_t=QG(t)^{-1}\varphi_M$ (invertible since $G$ is exact), a cone; with $t_0=\mathrm{id}$, $r=\varphi_M^{-1}$ and $k=t$ the pro condition of [def-pc-essentially-constant-pro-diagram] is $u_tr\,QG(t)=1$.

proof.text: For a complex $N$ choose a K-injective resolution $N\to I$ from step 7. Exactness makes $r_UN\to r_UI$ a quasi-isomorphism, and step 3 makes $r_UI$ K-injective. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] computes the two sides of $d_N$ as $Q(r_VF_SI)$ and $Q(F_Rr_UI)$ respectively. Define $d_N$ by $Q(q_I)$ under these computation isomorphisms. It is invertible. A morphism between K-injective representatives has a unique homotopy class representing a given derived morphism by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; naturality of $q$ makes this square commute on that class. Every derived object has such a representative, and a quasi-isomorphism between two of them is a homotopy equivalence by the same cited lemma. The comparisons therefore define a natural isomorphism on the whole derived category, independent of resolution through the canonical comparison maps. On $N=QI$ it is exactly the comparison induced by the underived identity required in the statement.

To check adjuncts, represent $M$ by a complex $C$ and $N$ by $QI$ with $I$ K-injective in the $S_U$ diagram category. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], $t$ is represented by a chain map $h:L_SC\to I$. Under the normalization formula in [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general], taking its source quasi-isomorphism to be the identity and its target to be this K-injective representative, $t^\sharp$ is represented by $f=F_S(h)\eta^S_C:C\to F_SI$, followed by the K-injective computation isomorphism. The same formula for $L_R\dashv RF_R$ computes the adjunct of $r_U(t)b_M^{-1}$ using $r_UI$, which is K-injective by step 3, as
$$F_R(r_U(h)(b^0_C)^{-1})\eta^R_{r_VC}.$$
Step 6 identifies this chain map with $q_Ir_V(f)$. Localizing and inserting exactly the computation isomorphisms used in step 8 gives $d_Nr_V(t^\sharp)$. Functoriality in both localized variables, included in the normalized-adjunction lemma, transports the equality back along the representing isomorphisms for $M,N$.

source.place: Tag 0FND, lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general, explicit representative formula; Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective

proof.text: All functors, resolutions and chain maps used above live in the category of $J$-diagrams. In particular $b^0$ and $q$ commute with the transition corresponding to $\alpha:j\to k$ by their module naturality; the degreewise maps in their complex versions retain that equality. The chosen resolutions are resolutions of diagrams, so their structure maps and comparison maps are diagram morphisms too. Localization is a functor and preserves these equalities. Thus $b,d$ and the adjunct equation are statements in derived diagram categories, with every transition retained; no reconstruction of a derived diagram from its separate evaluations was used.
